questions.question: Why do predators and prey have specialized physical or behavioral features?
options: To allow them to hibernate during the winter months
To help predators capture prey and help prey avoid being hunted
To ensure they can survive without any water or oxygen
To help them transition from producers into consumers

questions.question: Which of the following is a common adaptation that helps prey animals avoid being caught by predators?
options: Having large, sharp tearing teeth
Being active only during the day with bright, visible colors
Having good camouflage or being nocturnal
Developing the ability to photosynthesize

questions.question: Which set of features represents common adaptations found in predators to help them catch their food?
options: Soft bodies, slow movement, and dull senses
Big teeth, good eyesight, and the ability to run fast
Green leaves, deep roots, and seed production
Bright warning colors, small size, and living underground

questions.question: What happens to persistent toxic substances when an organism containing them is eaten by a predator?
options: They are completely broken down and rendered harmless by digestion.
They are excreted immediately without entering the predator's body.
They are passed up the food chain into the body of the predator.
They are converted into useful nutrients and energy.

questions.question: Which group of organisms in an ecosystem is typically most severely damaged by the bioaccumulation of toxic substances?
options: Producers at the start of the food chain
Decomposers in the soil
Primary consumers that feed on plants
Top predators at the end of the food chain

questions.question: What components make up a habitat where plants and animals live?
options: Only living (biotic) organisms
Only non-living (abiotic) physical factors
Both living (biotic) and non-living (abiotic) parts
Only human-made structures and concrete foundations

questions.question: Which of the following describes the role of producers in an ecosystem?
options: They must hunt other animals to obtain energy.
They make their own food, and include plants and some microorganisms.
They break down dead matter to return nutrients to the soil.
They feed exclusively on fruits and seeds produced by other plants.

questions.question: Why are animals, including humans, classified as consumers?
options: Because they can produce food using sunlight and carbon dioxide.
Because they cannot make their own food and must eat other organisms.
Because they release oxygen back into the atmosphere for plants.
Because they convert minerals directly into biomass without eating.

questions.question: In a food chain diagram, what do the arrows pointing from one organism to another represent?
options: The direction of movement and migration of the species
The transfers of biomass from one organism to the next
The relative physical size of each population
The amount of sunlight absorbed by each level

questions.question: What does a food web diagram represent in an ecosystem?
options: The physical pathways animals walk to find water holes
A single, linear sequence of who eats whom in a habitat
Several interconnected food chains within a community of organisms
The genetic relationships and evolutionary history of species

questions.question: Why do all consumers ultimately depend on producers for survival?
options: Producers release the carbon dioxide needed for consumers to breathe.
Producers make all of the food for the rest of the food chain.
Producers act as shelter and protection from all weather elements.
Producers control the temperature of the local environment.

questions.question: What is pollination, which leads to the production of edible seeds and fruits in plants?
options: The absorption of water and minerals through the root system
The release of oxygen from leaves during photosynthesis
The transfer of pollen from the anthers of flowers to the stigma
The dispersal of mature seeds by wind currents

questions.question: Why are pollinators vital for human food security?
options: They directly destroy weeds that compete with agricultural crops.
They ensure there is enough food to feed the human population by helping crops reproduce.
They purify drinking water reservoirs through their life cycles.
They add essential nitrates and minerals directly to the agricultural soil.

questions.question: What is meant by the term 'biodiversity'?
options: The total weight of all living organisms in a specific area
The rate at which plants produce biomass using photosynthesis
The number of different species that live in a place
The variation in climate conditions across different seasons

questions.question: How can genetic diversity of plant species be preserved for the future?
options: By increasing the usage of chemical pesticides on farms
Through seed banks and other forms of gene banks
By replacing natural habitats with monoculture crop fields
By introducing foreign predator species into local ecosystems

questions.question: How do insect-targeting pesticides help crops grow more efficiently?
options: By increasing the amount of sunlight the crop leaves can absorb
By directly supplying nutrients like nitrogen to the soil
By killing insects so that the crops are not being eaten
By encouraging insect pollinators to visit the crop flowers
